vizwiz_codes.BLR: blurry / out of focus / motion blur
vizwiz_codes.OBS: obstruction - finger or object partly covering the lens
vizwiz_codes.FRM: framing - subject cut off / incomplete / bad composition

mappings.reasoning: VizWiz BLR (blurry / out of focus / motion) is the same concept as VYRA 'blur'. Both defocus and motion blur are covered on each side.
'Too bright' corresponds to VYRA 'overexposure'. Slight gap: BRT can also be flagged for glare/reflections that are not global overexposure.
'Too dark' corresponds to VYRA 'underexposure'. Real dark images also carry heavy sensor noise, which VYRA models as a separate label.

OBS (finger/object over the lens) overlaps ONLY the 'occlusion' sub-type of VYRA's synthetic 'defect' (1 of 5 synthetic defect types). VYRA defect also covers dead pixels, banding, block corruption, colour blotches -- none of which VizWiz labels. Treated as a weak proxy, reported with heavy caveats.
Framing / subject cut off. VYRA has no framing concept and it is not an image-quality degradation in VYRA's taxonomy. Unmapped.
Wrong orientation. Not a VYRA concept and not a degradation. Unmapped.
Free-text 'other'. Too heterogeneous to map; kept only as context.
'No issue' vote count. Auxiliary: high NON is corroborating evidence for a clean image (used in analysis, not as a label).
VizWiz has no noise category. Real sensor noise is present in many dark images but is never annotated. Not directly supported by this dataset.
VizWiz has no compression / digital-corruption category. 'unrecognizable' is severity, not corruption (see note). Not directly supported by this dataset.
